issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class defines a quantity accessor named retrieveQuantity(), but the rest of the code (Stock.java in the template and the solution) expects getQuantity(). This inconsistent method name breaks compilation and conflicts with the problem statement's requirement to add getters for all private fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the quantity accessor in the template StockIngredient from retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (or add a public getQuantity() method that delegates to retrieveQuantity()). This will align the template with the Stock implementation, the solution, and the problem requirement to provide getters for private fields.

issues.description: The template defines a getter named retrieveQuantity() for StockIngredient, while the solution and other code (Stock) use the conventional name getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs students to "add getters for all the private fields" which implies standard getter names. This inconsistent identifier (retrieveQuantity vs getQuantity) creates a mapping and compilation confusion: students will see calls to getQuantity() in Stock and the solution but only find retrieveQuantity() in the template, making it unclear which getter to implement or modify.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template getter retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (or add getQuantity() delegating to retrieveQuantity()) so that the Stock class, the problem instruction about getters, and the solution consistently use getQuantity(). Ensure all references in template code use getQuantity().
